title: Affineness of a geometric strict-local base
statement: Let s:Spec Omega to S be a geometric point of a scheme S [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-geometric-point], A=S_(s) its strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], K any field, and u:Spec K to A. Then the fibre product A times_S Spec K, with the second map the composite of u and the structural map A to S [def-pc-fibre-product], is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Corrected Tag 0EZV proof, step 1; Tag 04HX, closed-point structure

proof.text: The strictly henselian local structure and the closed-point equation of strictHenselizationResidue show that the structural map sends the closed point above s. Choose an affine open chart Spec R to S at that point. Its inverse image contains the closed point of the local spectrum, so IsLocalRing.closedPoint_mem_iff identifies that open with the whole spectrum. Lift the structural map through the chart; lift the other leg by composition with u. The chart inclusion is a monomorphism, so the fibre product over Spec R is also a fibre product over S. All three schemes over the chart are affine. Mathlib gives affineness of their pullback, and the canonical isomorphism transfers it to the requested pullback.

lean.statement:
theorem strictLocalBase_isAffine {S : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (u : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme s) :
    IsAffine (pullback (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s)
      (u ≫ Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s))
